en.help.title: Deno Language Server (deno lsp)
en.help.message:
Deno's language server provides completion, diagnostics, hover, navigation and formatting for TypeScript and JavaScript.

Install the Deno runtime first:
  curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh
  brew install deno

How gvim chooses deno lsp:
  * Native auto-selection (core behaviour, not this helper plugin): when the probed workspace root (the root gvim opened or switched to) has deno.json/deno.jsonc, the Deno runtime is confirmed through the workspace authority under the workspace trust gate, lsp_enabled is true and the language is typescript/javascript, gvim selects deno lsp. It only applies to an LSP manager created for that exact workspace root; nested/per-file TS/JS roots keep their configured server. deno lsp is installed with auto_start: false, so nothing is spawned silently; Start/Restart LSP Server starts that manager.
  * If a TS/JS manager already existed before the async probe answer landed, it keeps its configured server for the session — a plain Start/Restart restarts that manager, not Deno; a new manager (fresh root/relaunch) uses the provider.
  * Explicit configuration wins and opts out: an "lsp" entry for typescript or javascript in config.json always wins and skips Deno auto-selection, as do enabled:false/disabled languages and lsp_enabled:false. tsx is untouched. Use the entries below when you want explicit deno lsp configuration.
  * This bundled plugin's enable/disable toggle only controls its copy/check/help commands. It does not control the native Deno auto-selection, which runs in core regardless of whether this helper plugin is loaded/enabled.
  * Check Project runs deno --version through the workspace authority (remote included); the plugin's local-only PATH lookup is never used for a presence decision.

Explicit configuration (opts out of native auto-selection; also needed when the auto conditions do not apply):

  "lsp": {
    "typescript": {
      "command": "deno", "args": ["lsp"], "auto_start": false,
      "root_markers": ["deno.json", "deno.jsonc"],
      "initialization_options": { "enable": true }
    },
    "javascript": {
      "command": "deno", "args": ["lsp"], "auto_start": false,
      "root_markers": ["deno.json", "deno.jsonc"],
      "initialization_options": { "enable": true }
    }
  }

Notes:
  * Deno: Check Project reports the project config and whether deno can run through the workspace authority (deno --version), so a remote workspace is checked on the remote host.
  * Deno LSP is started on demand once the deno provider is active: open a TypeScript/JavaScript file and use Start/Restart LSP Server.
  * Copy Install Command always copies the official curl installer; the popup also lists Homebrew for users who prefer it on their host.

Docs: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/getting_started/installation/
